newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere set to rise further in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Solidere set to rise further in Beirut.

text.p: Solidere shares rose 4.9 percent to $13.375 on Wednesday after recent profit taking brought the shares down from two-year record levels on the Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE).
Brokers said demand on Solidere would further strengthen in the coming period and that an upward trend has been set for the company shares.
"We are positive on the stock," Ziad Makkawi, of Middle East Capital Group, told Reuters.
Two bank shares, Banque Audi and Bank of Beirut were unchanged while Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce -- the third listed bank -- fell by 2.9 percent.
Banque Audi on Wednesday reported an 18.7 percent rise in net profits in the first half of 1997 to $11.05 million compared to the same period of last year.
The LIBX bank index fell 0.96 percent to 187.69. The BLOM general index rose 3.89 percent to 1136.71 and the LISPI general index increased 0.61 percent to 96.18.
BSE turnover rose 30 percent to 415,702 shares from 319,897 for a value of $5,383,159 against $3,915,546.
Solidere dominated market turnover with 356,502 shares changing hands.
"Finally, the market is gathering the necessary courage to get into what we believe to be the most undervalued stock in Lebanon," Makkawi added.
Both the company's A and B shares rose to $13.375 from $12.75 in heavy demand. Last Tuesday, the shares hit $13.75.
"It is not clear how high the share will go in the near future, but the trend is set," Makkawi said.
Banque Audi maintained its record high of $28.75 and Bank of Beirut was unchanged at $4.875. Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce fell to $21.375 from $22.
There was no trade in the other three industrial firms -- Ciments Blanc, Eternit and Uniceramic
